newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thousands march against Thomson sale to Daewoo.
newsitem.headline: Thousands march against Thomson sale to Daewoo.

text.p: Several thousand employees of French consumer electronics company Thomson Multimedia held protest marches in Paris and some other towns on Wednesday against the planned sale of the group to South Korea's Daewoo.
Workers of the state-owned company came in busloads to Paris to demonstrate in front of the group's headquarters in central Paris before heading to the parliament buildings.
Protest marches were also planned in Rennes, Bordeuax, Nice and Grenoble.
Thomson staff are dismayed that they have not been involved in the decision making about the state of the company and say they do not understand the economic logic behind it.
The French government on October 16 said it planned the sell the state-owned Thomson SA group to Lagardere Groupe for one franc after an 11 billion franc capital injection.

Lagardere will keep Thomson SA's 58 percent stake in defence electronics group Thomson-CSF and sell television set and video recorder maker Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo Electronics, also for one franc.
France's Privatisation Commission and the European Commission still have to approve the deal.

"What we want is a halt to the privatisation procedure and the start of serious discussions about the future of the electronics industry in this country," a labour union spokesman told France 2 television.
The Communist-led CGT wants to see a public sale of the Thomson Multimedia company on the market, with Lagardere taking a big stake.
French Industry Minister Franck Borotra said that the company was "loss making in an economic sense".

"Thomson Multimedia is a great company, but it is losing money because it does not have sufficient shareholders funds, has debts ... and is active on a very competitive market," he told an industry conference.

Soon-hoon Bae, chairman of Daewoo Electronics, told a French parliamentary commission on Tuesday afternoon that the South Korean group could float part of Thomson Multimedia on the share market when it had returned to profit.
He said Daewoo planned to invest 13 billion francs ($2.6 billion) in Thomson Multimedia, of which five billion would be invested in the next five years in France. ($ = 5.080 French Francs)
